text:
kate (Acme): Hey team, since switching to the latest JS SDK (v2.4.1) we're seeing a spike of 429s during peak traffic windows. Looks correlated with client-side retries — burst of retries seem to pile up and exhaust our per-minute quota. Can share logs if useful.

maria (Support): Sorry you're hitting that, kate. Can you paste one raw request/response pair (headers + body) and the client config you used for retries? Also what's your account quota and burst settings?

kate (Acme): Here's an example response header we captured:```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 11 Feb 2025 14:12:07 GMT
Retry-After: 30
X-Request-Id: rwd_ABC123
Content-Type: application/json
```and client snippet:```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, maxRetries: 5, backoff: { baseMs: 100 } });
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-mini', prompt });
```We're on the default quota (60 req/min) for the route.

maria (Support): thanks — that Retry-After 30s is important. By default the SDK uses an exponential retry policy and will ignore Retry-After in some older patch releases, and with 5 retries that can produce a quick fanout if many clients retry simultaneously.

devin (SDK): pinging in. In v2.4.1 the default is indeed maxRetries=5 with an exponential backoff (base 100ms, factor 2) and small jitter. We recently shipped that to improve transient success rates but didn't roll out strict Retry-After honoring in all codepaths. That can make clients hammer the API for non-idempotent operations.

kate (Acme): that's worrying because some of these endpoints trigger billing events on success. We saw a double-charge once when a retry completed after the server processed the first request but response got lost and a retry succeeded.

tyler (SRE): tagging in — duplicate billing is a known edge case when retries aren't guarded by idempotency. Two things to fix fast: (1) client-side respect for Retry-After header and (2) encourage use of Idempotency-Key header for mutating endpoints so server can dedupe.

maria (Support): For immediate mitigation: can you set maxRetries=1 or 0 in your client config, and set retryMode to 'respect-retry-after' if available? That should stop the burst while we triage.

kate (Acme): setting maxRetries=1 now. Also starting to add Idempotency-Key for each create call. Quick question: does Redwood server dedupe on Idempotency-Key automatically or do we need to register keys somewhere?

devin (SDK): server dedupe works if you send header `Idempotency-Key` (any opaque uniq string) for recognized mutating endpoints. The server stores the key and outcome for a short TTL (30m) and will return the previous response if it's seen the key before. Use a UUID per unique logical operation.

devin (SDK): also two notes: (a) our JS SDK change to respect Retry-After by default is in PR #482 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482) — backport planned to a patch release this week, (b) we'll also flip default maxRetries from 5 -> 3 and enable full jitter to reduce synchronized retry spikes.

maria (Support): kate — if you can, share a sample of your traffic pattern (requests/sec over a 5m window) and whether clients are concentrated behind a single CDN IP — that helps us decide whether to temporarily bump quota or apply a soft throttle.

kate (Acme): attaching a small excerpt: ```csv
timestamp,reqs/sec
14:11:00,8
14:11:10,10
14:11:20,12
14:11:30,18
14:11:40,30
14:11:50,40
```Most clients are mobile apps hitting your hosted API via same region; yes some NATing so source IPs cluster.

tyler (SRE): NAT clustering + clients doing retries = classic herd effect -> quota blowout. Short-term options: (A) support can request a quota bump for Acme for peak windows, (B) recommend client-side smoothing: random jitter + token-bucket local limiter per device, (C) deploy a 'cooldown' proxy that serializes requests per user.

maria (Support): I'm opening an escalation ticket to infra to review your quota and logging (ticket INF-9561). In the meantime, we strongly recommend:
- use `Idempotency-Key` for all mutating endpoints
- set `maxRetries` to 1 or 0 for endpoints that charge on success
- implement full jitter: backoff = random(0, base * 2^n)
- honour `Retry-After` header in client if present

kate (Acme): good list, doing that now. Any repro steps you want me to run?

devin (SDK): if you can reproduce consistently, capture a pcap or request traces with X-Request-Id and send them to support. Also try toggling `maxRetries` in a few test devices and observe success rate vs 429 rate. Example quick repro:
```bash
# high concurrency test script (be careful on prod)
for i in {1..200}; do node call-one.js &
done
```
call-one.js should call the same endpoint without Idempotency-Key to reproduce the duplicate processing scenario.

maria (Support): kate — once you confirm the mitigations, we'll coordinate with infra to either bump quota during your planned release or apply a short-term per-account backoff policy.

deploy-bot: 1799002360 - rolling restart of api-proxy cluster completed (reason: apply per-route throttling rules).

kate (Acme): noticed 429s dropped significantly after we lowered retries and added idempotency keys. Looks much better — thanks.

devin (SDK): we'll ship the backport today that: respects Retry-After headers, reduces default maxRetries, and changes to full jitter. I'll post the patch release number here once available.

maria (Support): INF-9561 updated: infra is going to monitor for next 48h and will consider a temporary quota increase if traffic remains high. If you see any doubled billing events, ping me immediately and include the X-Request-Id.

kate (Acme): will do. huge help, appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:

maria (Support): glad it helped — closing the thread for now, reopen if anything else crops up. :white_check_mark:
